title: DynamoDB: partition key, sort key and single-table design

videos.script: Quitanda's orders have outgrown the files of the first lessons. {{table}} The app has to show a customer their orders in a few milliseconds, all day long. That is DynamoDB's job, and it does it on one condition. Every fast read names a key. {{key}} The key has two halves. The partition key is hashed, and the hash decides where the item lives. The sort key keeps the items under one partition key in order, so a range of them is one read. {{collection}} So in DynamoDB you do not start from the entities. You start from the questions, written down before the table exists. {{patterns}} Then you build keys that answer them. One table holds a customer, their orders and every line of every order. They are sorted so that one query returns an order with its lines. {{single}} And you will meet the write that replaces an item without a word, and the condition that stops it. {{condition}}
